{"domain":"network","id":"RB-019","procedure":"1. Compare the load balancer idle timeout with the application HTTP keep-alive idle timeout.
2. If the application closes idle keep-alive connections before the load balancer does, the load balancer reuses a connection the application already closed: 'connection reset by peer', then 502 or 504.
3. Set the application keep-alive idle timeout above the load balancer idle timeout.
4. Long requests (exports) hitting 504 point at the load balancer idle timeout itself: raise it for that route.
5. Count the connection resets per upstream connection: when every reset hits a connection that sat idle, one side of the connection has a shorter idle timeout than the other. Reused idle connections are the only ones reset.","revision":"2025-02-14","services":"all","symptoms":"Intermittent 502 and 504 at the load balancer, more frequent at low traffic. 'connection reset by peer' in the load balancer and application logs. Pods Ready, no restart.","tags":"502 504 load balancer alb idle timeout keep-alive connection reset by peer upstream intermittent","title":"Intermittent 502/504 behind the load balancer","verification":"No 502/504 and no 'connection reset by peer' for 30 minutes of low traffic."}
